summary.oneLiner: NephroPlus (Nephrocare Health Services Limited) is India's and Asia's largest dialysis network and the world's fifth largest by treatment volume, operating 520+ clinics across five countries.
summary.business: NephroPlus offers comprehensive dialysis care through a network of clinics, from diagnosis to treatment and wellness, including hemodialysis, home and mobile dialysis, supported by pharmacy, diagnostics, renal nutrition counseling and mental-health support. It reaches guests through in-hospital captive clinics, standalone clinics and government-backed public-private partnerships (PPP) across India, Nepal, the Philippines, Uzbekistan and Saudi Arabia (via a JV).

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Centralized procurement of consumables and pharmaceuticals across clinics for uniform pricing and improved margins. Backward/vertical integration into key consumables: contract manufacturing arrangements for acid/bicarbonate (directly procures raw materials) and blood tubing sets (invested in proprietary moulds, sources tubing independently, engages contract manufacturers for assembly). Consumables as % of revenue fell from 32.59% (FY23) to 23.05% (H1FY26).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Dialysis is a chronic, life-sustaining treatment needed three times a week, every week, for life, giving the business unusually predictable, recurring, fixed-capacity ('airline-like') revenue.
- Large underserved global and Indian market: an estimated 25 million people worldwide lack access to dialysis; in India CKD affects close to 12.4 crore people, yet only about 7% are diagnosed, and of the roughly 42 lakh ESRD patients in 2024 only about 3 lakh received dialysis — the dialysis population is projected to grow from 3 lakh to 5.2 lakh by 2029, a CAGR of about 13%.
- Rising global and Indian burden of diabetes and hypertension — the two leading causes of CKD — is structurally expanding the addressable dialysis market as diagnosis rates rise.
- Asia will carry the major future CKD burden (an estimated 434 million adults with CKD) and is shifting toward organized care as governments raise healthcare spending and organized networks expand, while established markets like Japan and South Korea already show what universal access can look like.
- India's macro and healthcare-sector outlook remains supportive: strong GDP growth, rising disposable incomes, expanding urbanization, and expanding insurance coverage / government schemes (Ayushman Bharat, PM-JAY) support demand for organized private healthcare.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Three growth levers: steady ramp-up at existing clinics, roll-ups of clinics in countries where NephroPlus already operates, and entry into new countries or sizeable acquisitions.
- Continue expanding the dialysis network, enhance clinical excellence, invest in technology and digital healthcare solutions, strengthen the talent pool, and pursue strategic growth opportunities across India and selected international markets.
- Disciplined capital allocation framework, conservative provisioning, and a long-term view that places quality of earnings above short-term optimization; (adjusted) ROCE is management's primary filter for every rupee deployed.
- Technology as a key enabler for quality dialysis delivery — first global dialysis network to use AI in core operations, with the Reformmed.AI platform live across more than 50 clinics.
- Build a proprietary workforce pipeline through Enpidia, the training academy, a model now replicated in the Philippines.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: NephroPlus grows via three routes: greenfield clinics (average 5 beds, first-year run rate ~250 treatments), brownfield unit-by-unit roll-up (lower upfront investment, faster ramp-up, average ~10 beds leveraging an existing guest base and local staff), and acquisitions (network roll-up). Acquired clinics typically reach operational breakeven in three to four months versus roughly twelve months for a greenfield clinic. A dedicated 26-person business development team runs a structured M&A engine — comprehensive evaluation on infrastructure quality, clinical outcomes and regulatory compliance, review by an internal Investment Committee against ROCE and strategic filters, then integration onto RenAssure protocols and centralized procurement. Acquisition pace has increased over the past four years: 4 clinics acquired in FY2022-23, 12 in FY2023-24, 10 in FY2024-25 and 11 in FY2025-26. Geographic expansion is guided by a framework prioritizing geographies with demand depth/scale and political and regulatory stability. Internationally, the network has expanded through the acquisition of DaVita India and its subsidiaries, entry into Nepal, a Uzbekistan PPP tender (USD 75 million, 2022) with subsequent footprint expansion in Kungrad and Beruniy, entry into the Philippines with a growing number of bolt-on clinic acquisitions (becoming the 3rd largest dialysis network in the Philippines), and entry into Saudi Arabia via a JV with Al Faisaliah Group in 2023, later reconstituted as a 51:49 JV with the publicly listed Arabian International Healthcare Holding Company (Tibbiyah) in 2025, where a home dialysis license was obtained and treatments commenced. The Board has not recommended a dividend for FY2025-26 and intends to retain and reinvest profits toward future growth and expansion initiatives.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Market leadership: India's and Asia's largest dialysis network, world's fifth largest by treatment volume, with over 50% share of the Indian organized dialysis market
- Asset-light, capital-efficient operating model — ~52% of clinics under revenue-sharing arrangements with limited upfront investment, enabling high return on capital employed
- Cost leadership from operating in India at the world's lowest price point (USD 22 per treatment), driven by in-house manufacturing of key consumables and an in-house biomedical engineering team controlling the two largest cost levers
- Single-specialty focus with standardized, protocol-driven clinical approach applied consistently across every clinic
- Proprietary talent pipeline through Enpidia, its own dialysis training academy, replicated in the Philippines
- Technology and AI embedded across the dialysis journey, including the Reformmed.AI platform live across more than 50 clinics — the first global dialysis network to use AI in core operations
- Global procurement scale and a repeatable, proven expansion playbook (greenfield, brownfield roll-up and acquisitions) replicated across borders into higher-priced international markets
- Wide distribution reach: ~79% of clinics in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and towns, generating ~73% of revenue salience from those markets
- Only Indian dialysis network to have scaled internationally, now present in five countries

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- High treatment costs and affordability constraints — Per-session dialysis costs range from Rs 1,000-3,500, creating a financial burden for patients; lack of comprehensive insurance or low income limits access and increases mortality risk, impacting patient volumes.
- Geographic disparities and access gaps — Approximately 90% of dialysis facilities are located in urban areas while rural and semi-urban populations remain underserved; over 60% of patients travel more than 50 km for hemodialysis.
- Human resource shortage — India has approximately 2,600 nephrologists (1.90 per million population versus a global median of 9.95 per million), alongside a severe shortage of dialysis technicians and nurses and high attrition rates.
- Patient compliance and adherence — Only about 50% of Indian dialysis patients receive the WHO-recommended three treatments per week (47% receive two, the remainder one); poor adherence worsens outcomes and constrains revenue per patient.
- Regulatory and reimbursement risk — Complexity in regulatory approvals, delayed empanelment under government health schemes, and potential changes to reimbursement rates (PM-JAY, PhilHealth, Uzbekistan government rates) may impact revenue predictability.
- International expansion risk — Operations across diverse regulatory, currency and cultural environments in the Philippines, Uzbekistan, KSA and Nepal expose the Company to execution, integration, currency and political risks.
- Cybersecurity and data privacy risk — Increasing digital integration of patient records, IoT-enabled machines and teleconsultation platforms heightens cyber risk and data-privacy obligations across multiple jurisdictions.
